description:
The HUD velocity readout on /fly shows 'NaN km/s' for the entire cruise to any outer-planet destination (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, Ceres).

Expected: The HUD displays the spacecraft's heliocentric speed (km/s) at its current position on the transfer ellipse, using the correct destination-specific semi-major axis in vis-viva.

Acceptance criteria:
- heliocentricKms must be a finite number for every simDay on any mission trajectory to Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, or Ceres. [code-invariant: NaN is never a valid speed display; Math.sqrt of a negative number is always a bug.]
- the aTransferAu parameter passed to flyHeliocentricSpeed() for a non-Moon mission must be (R_EARTH_AU + DESTINATIONS[activeDestination].a) / 2, using the actual destination's semi-major axis, not hardcoded to the Earth-Mars average. [repo-data: static/data/planets.json provides per-planet 'a' (semi-major axis); DESTINATIONS table in lambert-grid.constants.ts exposes every destination's a; outboundArc() at src/lib/orbital/mission-arc.ts line 93 already computes the transfer-ellipse a as (R_EARTH_AU + destA) / 2 for the correct destination — the HUD formula must match.]
- For Mars missions, the current value ((R_EARTH_AU + R_MARS_AU) / 2) must remain correct — the fix must not regress Mars speeds. [repo-data: DESTINATIONS.mars.a === R_MARS_AU, so (R_EARTH_AU + DESTINATIONS['mars'].a) / 2 is numerically identical to the current expression. The formula generalises transparently.]
- For Moon missions, the current Earth-as-semi-major-axis behavior (isMoonMission ? R_EARTH_AU) must remain unchanged — the spacecraft co-orbits Earth. [spec: Comment at src/routes/fly/+page.svelte lines 942-948: 'For HUD honesty we use Earth's heliocentric radius for vis-viva so HELIO ΔV reads ~29.78 km/s consistently (the spacecraft co-orbits with Earth around the Sun during the transit).']

Domain facts:
- Earth semi-major axis ≈ 1.000 AU (R_EARTH_AU)
- Mars semi-major axis ≈ 1.524 AU (R_MARS_AU)
- (R_EARTH_AU + R_MARS_AU) / 2 ≈ 1.262 AU → 2a ≈ 2.524 AU is the NaN threshold
- Jupiter a=5.203 AU, Saturn a=9.537 AU, Uranus a=19.191 AU, Neptune a=30.069 AU, Pluto a=39.482 AU — all far exceed 2.524 AU
- DESTINATIONS[activeDestination].a is already available at the call site (DESTINATIONS is imported at line 65, activeDestination is in scope as $state at line 300)
